```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
can_report <- rlang::is_installed(c("gtsummary", "cardx", "survey", "gt"))
```

easyNIS takes you from annual National Inpatient Sample (NIS) Parquet files to
a survey-weighted table, with primary small cells suppressed. This guide
walks through the steps on `nis_example()` data: invented discharges that have
the NIS column layout but no real records. Replace the example path with the
directory that holds your own `NIS_<year>.parquet` files to run a real study.

## Open the data

`nis_open()` opens the annual files lazily, so nothing is read into memory
until you ask for it. Mixed-case NIS column names are normalized across years;
wholly lower-case names are left unchanged.

```{r open}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path)

nis |>
  dplyr::count(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

## Flag diagnoses and procedures

`nis_flag_dx()` and `nis_flag_pr()` add one logical column per named set of
ICD-10 code prefixes. Each diagnosis or procedure slot is checked on its own,
and the work stays lazy. Prefixes ignore case, periods, and spaces; stored
codes must use the NIS upper-case, period-free layout.

```{r flag}
nis <- nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(
    heart_failure = "I50",
    palliative_care = "Z515"
  ) |>
  nis_flag_pr(ablation = "02L")

nis |>
  dplyr::count(heart_failure, palliative_care) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Use `position = "principal"` to look at the principal diagnosis only. To
build the prefix lists from an HCUP CCSR reference file that you download
yourself, see `nis_ccsr_codes()`.

## Build the survey design

`nis_design()` takes a cohort expression and the columns to keep, collects the
cohort, and returns a nested survey design. It adds a placeholder row for each
hospital-year with no cohort discharges, so variance estimates account for the
whole sample. It also labels coded fields, and, when `TOTCHG` and `CCR_NIS` are
kept, adds inflation-adjusted `cost_adj` and `charges_adj`.

```{r design}
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, DIED, LOS, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS, palliative_care),
  dollars = 2024
)
```

Discharges with a missing or invalid design field are excluded with a
warning that gives their number. The design-based tools in the survey and
srvyr packages work on the result as they would on any other design.

```{r summarise}
srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS)
)
```

## Table 1 and a model

`gtsummary::tbl_svysummary()` builds a weighted table from the design, and
`survey::svyglm()` fits a model that uses the survey structure.

The table chunks need the optional gtsummary, cardx, survey, and gt packages.
Install them before running this guide if they are not already available.

```{r table, eval=can_report}
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = palliative_care,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, cost_adj)
) |>
  gtsummary::add_overall()
```

```{r model, eval=rlang::is_installed("survey")}
fit <- survey::svyglm(
  LOS ~ palliative_care + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design
)

summary(fit)
```

## Suppress small cells

HCUP data use agreements require suppressing cells that describe 10 or fewer
discharges. `nis_suppress()` masks displayed statistics whose unweighted count
is at or below the threshold and adds a footnote that says so. It masks
primary cells only, so check related totals before you publish.

```{r suppress, eval=can_report}
nis_suppress(table_one, threshold = 10)
```

## Start a study folder

`nis_new_study()` copies a Quarto template to a new directory. The template
reproduces the steps above as a report with cohort flow, Table 1, outcomes,
yearly trends, and regression tables. Its `analysis.qmd` runs on invented data
until you set its `data_path` parameter.

```{r new-study}
study <- tempfile("my-nis-study-")
nis_new_study(study)
list.files(study, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
```

Edit the definitions block in `analysis.qmd` for your cohort, then render it
with Quarto.

## Where next

The "Porting an existing NIS study to easyNIS" vignette maps common
regular-expression and recoding steps to easyNIS. `nis_reweight()` applies
propensity weights to a design, and `nis_comorbidity()` adds AHRQ Elixhauser
columns; both are experimental.
